title: Implement two-parabolic-band material model and generate silicide property curves
action: Implement the two-parabolic-band semiconductor model (acoustic-phonon scattering factor -1/2, alloy scattering with T^{-1/2} dependence, mobility T^{-3/2} for acoustic) for n-type silicide Mg2Si0.4Sn0.6 using the equations from the Supplementary Information. Use the fixed material parameters from Table 2 (doping around 3.7e20 cm⁻³ as reference, then a range of doping concentrations covering both efficiency-optimal and peak-ZT-optimal regimes). For each doping, solve the charge neutrality condition to obtain the Fermi level at each temperature, then compute the Seebeck coefficient, electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, and ZT from 30 °C to at least 450 °C at 5 °C intervals. Save the temperature-dependent arrays in a structured file for the next step.
description: Mandatory intermediate that produces the α(T), σ(T), κ(T), ZT(T) curves required by the efficiency calculation. The evidence file is an optional artifact documenting the run.

title: Compute single-leg efficiency and compile doping-dependent data
action: For each doping concentration, use the material property curves from the model output to compute the steady-state thermoelectric efficiency of a single n-type leg with hot-side 400 °C and cold-side 30 °C, assuming ideal electrical and thermal contacts. Use a 1D finite‑element/finite‑difference solver or an analytic integral formula that accounts for temperature-dependent properties and the Thomson effect (open‑source alternative to COMSOL). Also compute the peak ZT (maximum over the temperature range) and the average ZT (arithmetic mean from 30 °C to 400 °C). Write the results to a CSV file.
description: Scored CSV containing the raw doping-dependent quantities. The checker verifies doping ranking and structural relationships (efficiency-optimal doping has lower peak ZT and higher average ZT).

title: Extract and compare optimal dopings and quantify trade-off
action: From the doping‑dependent data in step_01_efficiency_data.csv, identify the doping that maximizes efficiency and the doping that maximizes peak ZT. Compute the efficiency at both dopings and the peak ZT at both dopings. Calculate the percentage increase in peak ZT when going from the efficiency‑optimal doping to the peak‑ZT‑optimal doping, and the percentage decrease in efficiency for the same transition. Write a JSON file with the results.
description: Scored JSON containing the quantified trade‑off. The checker compares the reported peak_ZT_increase_pct and efficiency_decrease_pct to the paper’s gold values (19% and 16%) within a ±3% tolerance.
output_schema: efficiency_optimal_doping (float), peak_ZT_optimal_doping (float), efficiency_at_peak_ZT_optimal (float), efficiency_at_efficiency_optimal (float), peak_ZT_at_efficiency_optimal (float), peak_ZT_at_peak_ZT_optimal (float), peak_ZT_increase_pct (float), efficiency_decrease_pct (float)
